definitions.explanation: A negative evaluation or reception of something. Used when a product, decision, or action is poorly received by others.

examples.japanese: その{計画|けいかく}は{不評|ふひょう}だった。
{新|あたら}しいデザインが{社員|しゃいん}に{不評|ふひょう}で、{変更|へんこう}された。
examples.english: The new design was unpopular with employees and was changed.

examples.japanese: {値上|ねあ}げが{消費者|しょうひしゃ}の{間|あいだ}で{大|おお}いに{不評|ふひょう}を{買|か}っている。
examples.english: The price increase is drawing a great deal of criticism from consumers.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used with を{買|か}う (to draw criticism/unpopularity) as a set expression. Can function as a な-adjective ({不評|ふひょう}な{映画|えいが} — an unpopular movie).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不評|ふひょう}を{買|か}う (to draw criticism, to be poorly received)
- {不評|ふひょう}だった (was unpopular)
- {不評|ふひょう}な{意見|いけん} (an unpopular opinion)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {好評|こうひょう}: good reputation, popularity — the direct opposite
- {評判|ひょうばん}: reputation — neutral, can be good or bad
